content: Hello! how can I help today?
I’m the trustee of a family trust. Do I have to file a separate tax return?
Yes. Most irrevocable trusts must file **Form 1041** if they have more than $600 of gross income or any taxable income. The trust is a separate tax entity.
Can the trust pass income to the beneficiaries?
Yes. If the trust distributes income, it takes a deduction and the beneficiaries report the income via **Schedule K-1**. The trust only pays tax on income it retains.
Is the trust tax rate the same as individuals?
No. Trusts hit the highest tax bracket very quickly. For 2024, only $15,200 of taxable income puts a trust in the 37% bracket. It’s more tax-efficient to distribute income when possible.
Each beneficiary receives a **Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)**. It shows their share of income, deductions, and credits from the trust. They use it to report on their personal Form 1040.
